t: Find the Sum of Encrypted Integers
o: encrypt(x) replaces every digit of x with its largest digit: encrypt(523) = 555. We sum encrypt over all elements. With values ≤ 1000 and at most 50 numbers, per-number digit inspection is instantaneous. For 10, 21, 31 the results are 11, 22, 33, summing to 66.
k: Encryption depends only on the maximum digit d and the digit count L: result = d repeated L times.
Equivalently result = d · repunit(L) where repunit(L) = 111…1 (L ones).
Constraints are tiny; string handling is the simplest implementation.

a.i: Convert each number to a string, find its max character, and rebuild the number as that digit repeated. Sum the results.
s: For each x, take its decimal string s.
Let d = max digit of s.
Add int(d repeated len(s) times) to the answer.
a.t: O(S) where S is the total number of digits — at most 50 × 4 digits.
a.sp: O(1) auxiliary (O(L) for the string form).

w: Trivial problem; the only care point is building the repeated-digit number correctly (repunit trick avoids string allocation in compiled languages). Edge cases: single-digit numbers encrypt to themselves. A likely follow-up asks for the sum modulo something with huge inputs — then compute d · repunit(L) mod p arithmetically.
